svg.title: Risk tiers and human approval
svg.desc: Engraved plate of three pedestals of rising height for the risk tiers. Low: docs, copy, internal-only code, additive behaviour behind a flag; 0 human approvals once AI review and security are green. Medium: ordinary product changes and sensitive areas such as caching, auto-updater and system prompts; 1 human approval. High: billing, auth, migrations and a small set of paths that always need two; 2 human approvals. Each approval is drawn as a seal. The change sets the tier, not the author. Rules: highest path wins; the second opinion can only raise the need for a person; CI workflow files always need a person; agent and bot approvals are not human approvals; approvals are dismissed on new commits. Source: A. Osmani, M. W. Lunt and Q. Wang, “How the Claude Code team does code review”, Anthropic, 15 October 2026, https://claude.dev/blog/solving-code-review-at-anthropic/. Independent implementation, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
